thumbnail_brief: Night, a lantern-lit canvas tent seen from outside with two big, lean, maneless lion heads pushing through the flap, eyes lit and blank (never cute or smiling), and tiny Doug in a camp bed inside with the blanket to his chin looking at the camera, so the title's '9 months of killing' gets its twist from NO MANES (never TSAVO, LIONS, KILLING, WORKERS, MONTHS, MAN-EATER, a victim count or a price; no blood, no rifles, no victims drawn).
description:
In 1898 the Tsavo lions, two maneless males, hunted the workers building a British colonial railway bridge in Kenya for nine months, walking through thorn fences and campfires until hundreds of workers stopped a train and left. Doug joins the Tsavo man-eaters' camp from the first week to the last night, while the lions' own hair, bones and broken teeth show about how many people they actually ate, and why.

Where should we send Doug next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe. Doug's death counter only goes up, and the lions never needed a reason.
